concepts.definition: Canonical typed compute composition generated exactly by C.of, C.id, C.compose, C.edge, workflow.C, C.batch and C.retry; transform/evaluate/consequence is bootstrap algebra data rather than a closed stage ontology.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-001 - Closed generator set.** The compute algebra
generator set is exactly `C.of`, `C.id`, `C.compose`, `C.edge`, `workflow.C`,
`C.batch`, and `C.retry`. A build tenant shall represent the set with an
exhaustively matchable typed carrier. The canonical transform/evaluate/
consequence edge is bootstrap data expressed by the algebra, not a closed stage
ontology.

concepts.label: Compute C term

concepts.definition: One C.of<A,B,Role,Fibre> leaf with one C-call spine; its role, fibre, arm and carrier references combine with the enclosing CProgramDeclaration.programRef to identify one program/role/fibre/arm census member.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-002 - Unit.**
`C.of<A,B,Role,Fibre>(stage<A,B,Role,Fibre>) -> C<A,B>` introduces one atomic
C-call leaf. The enclosing `CProgramDeclaration.programRef` supplies program
identity; the leaf supplies role, fibre, arm, and input/output carrier refs.
Together they name one `(program, role, fibre, arm)` census member. The leaf
has one C-call spine and an implementation may realize only its interior.

concepts.label: Atomic C-call stage

concepts.definition: A plugin or handler realization of a declared leaf interior, matched to program identity, role, fibre, arm and its own published seam carrier contract, with no runtime-truth authority.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-010 - Implementation matching.** A plugin or handler
binding shall match the enclosing program identity and selected stage role,
fibre, and arm. C input/output carrier continuity is a GTL-validator
judgment. Each implementation separately matches the published carrier
contract of its plugin or handler seam; a uniform engine-plugin transport
carrier is not falsely equated with the domain C carrier ref. Its public type
and admitted carrier shall not provide event emission, traversal selection,
continuation, ledger, or closure authority. ABG admits its result and owns all
resulting runtime truth.

concepts.label: Implementation binding

concepts.definition: One subjectRef-bound admitted module/program/graph-function/catalog root and declared expected-coverage contract; reachability and applicable inventory fields determine the validator report scope.

grounding.quote:
A conformance report is scoped to one admitted submitted root identified by
`subjectRef`: its admitted module, program, graph-function, and catalog rows, plus its
declared expected-coverage contract. The GTL validator checks every declaration
reachable from that root and reports required rows missing relative to that
bound coverage contract where the contract carries an applicable inventory
field. For execution declarations, the validator proves declared-reference
completeness and internal membership; the current coverage carrier does not
express a total expected execution-declaration inventory. Product/install
binding selects the authoritative root and complete release manifest. Those
are separate release contracts.

concepts.label: Admitted submitted conformance root

concepts.definition: compose(f,g) creates a new graph function with f.inputs and g.outputs when f carries the cumulative environment required by g.

grounding.quote: Define lawful graph-function composition in GTL 3.

**REQ-L-GTL3-COMPOSE-001**: `compose(f, g)` shall compose two graph functions when `g.environment.requires` is satisfied by the cumulative environment carried by `f`. The result is a new graph function with `inputs = f.inputs` and `outputs = g.outputs`.

concepts.label: Graph-function composition

concepts.definition: fn<A,B>.C, transform.C, evaluate.C and consequence.C denote knowledge states and selected abg.fn_composition contract identity over existing lawful carriers; they add no literal language extension, topology object, runtime carrier or execution target.

grounding.quote:
Define the GTL-facing epistemology over the ratified GTL ontology and ABG
runtime ontology without adding a new GTL topology object, ABG runtime carrier,
or execution target.

The notation exists so authors and tools can distinguish what exists from how
it is known. Ontology names the lawful carriers. Epistemology names the
knowledge states over those carriers: candidate production, evaluation
findings, ABG admission, ABG ledger/projection truth, assurance fold,
traversal transition, and downstream consequence projection.

This requirement governs notation such as `fn<A, B>.C`, `transform.C`,
`evaluate.C`, and `consequence.C`, and the ontology/epistemology boundary those
terms rely on.

It is notation over existing GTL ontology and ABG runtime truth. It is not a
literal GTL language extension and not a second public carrier.

`C` is selected composition notation: the selected `abg.fn_composition`
contract identity for the owning boundary.

concepts.label: Compute epistemic notation

concepts.definition: GTL owns authored Graph, Node, GraphVector, Context, Operator, Evaluator, Rule, GraphFunction, RefinementBoundary, CandidateFamily, ContractRef, Role, Job and Module. ABG owns admitted composition, events, Run, GraphCall, Frame, ExecutionBasis, AdvancementTransition, IterationAdvanceDecision, Continuation, payload admission/ledgers, assurance/closure and traversal/replay. Product pressure maps, acceptance lenses, lifecycle registers and domain read models remain Product projections over admitted facts.

grounding.quote:
GTL ontology contains the authored language carriers:

- `Graph`
- `Node`
- `GraphVector`
- `Context`
- `Operator`
- `Evaluator`
- `Rule`
- `GraphFunction`
- `RefinementBoundary`
- `CandidateFamily`
- `ContractRef`
- `Role`
- `Job`
- `Module`

ABG runtime ontology contains ABG-admitted runtime truth, including:

- selected `abg.fn_composition`
- runtime events
- `Run`
- `GraphCall`
- `Frame`
- `ExecutionBasis`
- `AdvancementTransition`
- `IterationAdvanceDecision`
- `Continuation`
- payload admission and payload ledgers
- assurance projection and closure fold
- traversal transition and replay projection

Product ontology remains outside GTL and ABG. A downstream product may define
pressure maps, acceptance lenses, lifecycle registers, and domain read models,
but those meanings are product projections over ABG-admitted facts, not new GTL
or ABG ontology.

concepts.label: GTL, ABG and Product ontology partition

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-001 - Closed generator set.** The compute algebra
generator set is exactly `C.of`, `C.id`, `C.compose`, `C.edge`, `workflow.C`,
`C.batch`, and `C.retry`. A build tenant shall represent the set with an
exhaustively matchable typed carrier. The canonical transform/evaluate/
consequence edge is bootstrap data expressed by the algebra, not a closed stage
ontology.

**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-002 - Unit.**
`C.of<A,B,Role,Fibre>(stage<A,B,Role,Fibre>) -> C<A,B>` introduces one atomic
C-call leaf. The enclosing `CProgramDeclaration.programRef` supplies program
identity; the leaf supplies role, fibre, arm, and input/output carrier refs.
Together they name one `(program, role, fibre, arm)` census member. The leaf
has one C-call spine and an implementation may realize only its interior.

constraints.statement: Every tenant represents exactly the seven C generators in an exhaustively matchable typed carrier. One C.of supplies one atomic spine, and an implementation can realize only its interior.

conditions: no_declared_check requires an owning contract that demands no check.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-003 - Identity.** `C.id<A> -> C<A,A>` is the left and
right identity of composition. It projects `no_declared_check` only where the
owning contract demands no check. It cannot satisfy a required gate and cannot
make an otherwise empty executable edge program complete.

constraints.statement: C.id<A> is C<A,A> and the left/right composition identity. It projects no_declared_check only where the owning contract requires no check; it cannot satisfy a mandatory gate or complete an otherwise empty executable edge program.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-004 - Composition.**
`C.compose<A,B,D>(C<A,B>, C<B,D>) -> C<A,D>` is closed and associative.
Composition is flat by default: nested syntax erases to the ordered `C.of`
leaves in one declared boundary. Input/output mismatch is a type error where
the host language can decide it and otherwise a typed GTL-validator gap.

constraints.statement: C.compose<A,B,D> is closed and associative. Nested syntax flattens by default into ordered C.of leaves within one declared boundary. Input/output mismatch is a host type error where decidable and otherwise a typed GTL-validator gap.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-005 - Edge record.** `C.edge` is the named record form
of a composition containing transform, evaluate, and consequence roles. The
three fields are atomic direct `C.of` leaves with the corresponding stage-role
literal; wrapping or composition occurs outside the record. The roles remain
ordinary declared stages. Open programs may contain other non-empty roles and
shall name exactly one result-bearing role.

constraints.statement: C.edge records transform, evaluate and consequence fields as atomic direct C.of leaves with matching literal roles. Wrapping/composition is outside the record. Roles are ordinary open declaration data; other nonempty roles are permitted, but every open program names exactly one result-bearing role.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-006 - Named workflow lift.**
`workflow.C(GraphFunctionRef<A,B>) -> C<A,B>` is the only constructor that
makes an admitted graph-function traversal one transparent C at its parent
level. The typed `GraphFunctionRef` binds the admitted graph function and the
declared C input/output carriers; the lift preserves that `A,B` pair. Raw
validation proves that the named graph function resolves. Equality between
those carrier refs and a child's published wire contract requires an admitted
outer-contract identity and shall not be inferred when that identity is absent.
The lift yields `sub_traversal` evidence. Anonymous nesting never creates a
frame or monad boundary.

constraints.statement: Only workflow.C(GraphFunctionRef<A,B>) lifts an admitted graph-function traversal into one transparent parent-level C, preserving the reference-declared A,B pair and yielding sub_traversal evidence. Raw validation proves resolution, not equality to a child published wire contract without an admitted outer-contract identity. Anonymous nesting creates no frame or monad boundary.

conditions: Pointwise distribution requires equal-length compatible ordered task families.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-007 - Batch.** `C.batch(tasks, batchRef)` groups a
non-empty ordered task family whose members have the same input carrier,
output carrier, and per-task result cardinality. Stable list position pairs
tasks when applying a pointwise distributive law. The batch preserves one
C-call spine and one result-cardinality judgment per invoking task plus one
non-authoritative parent grouping ref; its program cardinality is that shared
per-task cardinality, not an aggregate `many`. Batch distributes over
composition only for equal-length compatible task families paired by stable
position. A batch never collapses task identity, evidence, or judgment into
one synthetic call.

constraints.statement: C.batch groups a nonempty ordered task family with equal input/output carriers and per-task result cardinality. Each invoking task retains one spine and one cardinality judgment; the parent grouping reference has no authority. Program cardinality stays the common per-task cardinality, not aggregate many. Distribution over composition requires equal-length compatible families paired by stable list position; task identity, evidence and judgments never collapse into one call.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-008 - Retry.** `C.retry(C<A,B>, budget) -> C<A,B>`
preserves the input/output contract and closes attempts under the one declared
retryable-failure allowlist. The budget is a positive declared value. Retry
does not create a per-fibre error algebra or authorize undeclared repair.

constraints.statement: C.retry preserves input/output contract, uses a positive declared budget and closes attempts under the single declared retryable-failure allowlist. It neither creates per-fibre error algebras nor authorizes undeclared repair.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-009 - Role/fibre orthogonality.** Stage role is open
declared program data. Fibre is one of `F_D`, `F_P`, or `F_H`. Substituting a
lawful fibre changes the selected interior and evidence class only; it does not
change graph topology, program membership, spine kinds, spine order, or spine
count. The GTL validator, HoG, and ABG preserve the declared fibre and never
reclassify semantic `F_P` work as `F_D` from observed behavior. Replacing a
prior `F_P` declaration with `F_D` is a declaration-version and annealing
decision governed by the tuner/equivalence requirements, not a local validator
inference.

constraints.statement: Stage roles are open program data; fibres are exactly F_D, F_P and F_H. Lawful substitution changes interior and evidence class only, preserving topology, program membership and spine kinds/order/count. Validator, HoG and ABG preserve the declared fibre; observed behavior cannot reclassify F_P as F_D. Prior F_P-to-F_D replacement requires declaration versioning and tuner/equivalence annealing.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-010 - Implementation matching.** A plugin or handler
binding shall match the enclosing program identity and selected stage role,
fibre, and arm. C input/output carrier continuity is a GTL-validator
judgment. Each implementation separately matches the published carrier
contract of its plugin or handler seam; a uniform engine-plugin transport
carrier is not falsely equated with the domain C carrier ref. Its public type
and admitted carrier shall not provide event emission, traversal selection,
continuation, ledger, or closure authority. ABG admits its result and owns all
resulting runtime truth.

constraints.statement: Implementation matching includes program/role/fibre/arm. GTL validates C carrier continuity separately from each implementation matching its seam contract; generic transport carriers must not be equated to domain C carrier references. Public/admitted bindings confer no event emission, traversal selection, continuation, ledger or closure authority. ABG admits results and owns resulting runtime truth.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-011 - No rival execution declaration.** The admitted
GTL program, its C declaration, GraphFunction templates, and implementation
bindings are the complete execution declaration. `abg.hog_program`,
`abg.hog_program_catalog`, `abg.hog_program_ref`,
`abg.hog_program_ladder`, generated handler-program declarations, or any
equivalent compiled runtime program shall be rejected as executable authority.
Implementation bindings may identify declared leaf seams only. Opaque
extension data shall not acquire runtime meaning by convention.

constraints.statement: The admitted GTL program, C declaration, GraphFunction templates and implementation bindings fully declare execution. Reject abg.hog_program, catalog/ref/ladder variants, generated handler-program declarations and equivalent compiled runtime programs as executable authority. Bindings identify only declared leaf seams; opaque extension data gains no conventional runtime meaning.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-012 - Native-language maximum.** Each conforming build
tenant shall use its native static type system and API patterns as far as they
can decide the law: discriminated unions, generic input/output relations,
nominal or opaque admitted states, exhaustive matching, constructor-only
creation, and role/fibre/host-indexed bindings. The GTL validator shall not
be used as an excuse to erase locally decidable types into strings or bags.

constraints.statement: Use native static type/API capabilities to the full extent they can decide law, including discriminated unions, generic I/O, opaque/nominal admitted states, exhaustive matching, constructor-only creation and role/fibre/host-indexed bindings. Do not erase locally decidable types into strings or bags by deferring to the validator.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-013 - Canonical-data admission.** Authored GTL remains
canonical pure data. Untyped files, generated data, package input, and API
payloads enter through raw admission that applies the same sort and relation
judgments as the native typed API. Native callers use the published typed
constructors; serialized callers use raw admission. Authored, admitted,
validated, and runtime values remain distinct states. A deterministic
native constructor is lawful only as a projection into that canonical data:
serialization plus raw readmission must preserve the exact value and digest.
Its loops, branching, and string construction do not become declaration
authority and may not consult ambient or runtime truth.

constraints.statement: Authored GTL is canonical pure data. Native callers use typed constructors; files, generated/package input and API payloads use raw admission with the same sort/relation judgments. Authored, admitted, validated and runtime states stay distinct. A deterministic native constructor is lawful only if serialization/raw readmission preserves exact value and digest; its loops, branches and strings gain no authority and cannot consult ambient/runtime truth.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-014 - Semantic gap ownership.** The GTL validator shall
decide closed facts that a local host type cannot: decoded input, references
reachable from the submitted root, program and catalog membership, carrier
continuity, result cardinality, constructor coverage, and implementation-seam
declaration completeness. Runtime admission shall decide environment-specific
availability and probabilistic result facts. A lawful term with no admitted
realization produces `semantic_not_realized`; an unresolved named reference
produces `invalid_program`; neither is silently lowered into another term or
compiled plan.

constraints.statement: The validator decides closed facts beyond local types: decoded data, root-reachable references, program/catalog membership, carriers, cardinality, constructor coverage and seam declaration completeness. Runtime admission decides environmental availability and probabilistic result facts. Lawful unrealized terms return semantic_not_realized; unresolved named references return invalid_program. Neither may silently lower to another term or compiled plan.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-015 - LLM repair protocol.** C-algebra conformance
failures shall carry a stable diagnostic identity, subject path, governing
axiom and requirement refs, evidence, and admissible repair moves. Direct
execution-declaration admission shall carry a stable typed refusal prefix and
reason before effects. Rich C diagnostics name the expected and actual sort or
relation; generic declaration diagnostics may use their stable rule, message,
evidence, and repair fields. Repair moves identify lawful constructors,
declaration surfaces, reference corrections, or constitutional re-entry. They
do not select, perform, or authorize a repair.

constraints.statement: C conformance failures carry stable diagnostic identity, subject path, governing axiom/requirement references, evidence and admissible repair moves. Execution-declaration admission carries typed refusal prefix/reason before effects. Rich C diagnostics name expected/actual sort or relation; generic diagnostics may use stable rule, message, evidence and repair fields. Suggested constructors, surfaces, reference corrections or constitutional re-entry do not select, perform or authorize repair.

exceptions: Diagnostic fail-closed events may report the refusal and terminal stop.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-016 - Validate before effects.** A program with a local
type failure, admission failure, or unresolved semantic gap shall stop before
worker/plugin invocation, archive writes, traversal, or successful assessment
or closure truth. Diagnostic fail-closed events may report the typed refusal
and terminal stop. HoG shall traverse only the original admitted GTL terms. It
shall not parse new program meaning, infer types from observed behavior, or
repair declarations. Validation and traversal admission preserve every
authored C stage, its order, role, fibre, arm, carriers, and result-bearing
designation. HoG- and ABG-owned call preparation, result admission, evidence
binding, and materialization are subordinate runtime transitions. They may
surround an authored stage but shall not form a rival runtime plan or replace,
rename, reorder, or count as authored program membership.

constraints.statement: Local type/admission failures and unresolved semantic gaps stop before worker/plugin calls, archive writes, traversal, successful assessment or closure. Diagnostic fail-closed events may report refusal and terminal stop. HoG traverses original admitted terms only and cannot parse new meaning, infer behavioral types or repair declarations. Preserve every stage, order, role, fibre, arm, carrier and result-bearing designation. HoG/ABG preparation, result admission, evidence binding and materialization may surround a stage only as subordinate transitions, never replace/reorder/rename/count as authored membership or a rival plan.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-017 - Conformance corpus.** The language conformance
corpus shall pair canonical positive and negative LLM-authored programs with
exact expected diagnostic identities. It shall cover sort coercion, interface
mismatch, role/fibre confusion, implementation mismatch, illegal declaration
host, duplicate authority, malformed serialized data, required declarations
named by declared references but absent from the submitted root, inferred
undeclared terms, every realized algebra law above, and stable
`semantic_not_realized` results for lawful unrealized constructors.

constraints.statement: Pair positive/negative LLM-authored programs with exact expected diagnostics covering sort coercion, interfaces, role/fibre and implementation mismatch, illegal declaration hosts, duplicate authority, malformed serialized data, missing root-required declarations, inferred undeclared terms, every realized law and stable semantic_not_realized for lawful unrealized constructors.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-018 - F_P response admission.** The standard `F_P`
transform, runtime-failure, and live-evaluator responses used by this execution
surface are data until ABG admits their closed schemas, required identities and
evidence references, and cross-field invariants. Attached result artifacts
admit their base envelope and closed assessment rows while domain extension
sections remain governed by the selected declared artifact schema. Malformed
output produces a typed blocked or rejected result. Incomplete or contradictory
evaluation output produces retry or blocked truth, never accepted closure by
omission. Raw diagnostic evidence may be retained. This is model-output
validation, not hostile-process tamper protection.

constraints.statement: F_P transform, runtime-failure and live-evaluator outputs remain data until ABG checks closed schemas, required identities/evidence references and cross-field invariants. Attached artifacts admit base envelopes and closed assessment rows; declared artifact schemas govern domain extensions. Malformed outputs are blocked/rejected, and incomplete/contradictory evaluation yields retry or blocked truth, never closure by omission. Raw diagnostics may remain. This is output validation, not hostile-process protection.

grounding.quote:
The current product is a single-developer desktop tool. Native code running in
the process and values already returned by the published typed constructors are
trusted. This requirement does not require tamper-proofing against hostile
in-process code, reflected private fields, forged local objects, filesystem
attackers, or cryptographic artifact substitution.

Malformed authored GTL is expected and shall be rejected by native type
matching, raw admission, lint/source guards, or GTL validation at the
earliest boundary capable of deciding the fault. `F_P` output is probabilistic
external data and remains subject to its published result-schema admission and
contradiction checks before ABG projects accepted assessment or closure truth.
Raw observed/diagnostic evidence and non-close retry truth may be retained.
This requirement owns the declaration and implementation match leading to that
seam; the applicable ABG plugin/result requirement owns the returned-output
schema.

constraints.statement: The specified single-developer desktop model trusts in-process native code and values returned by published typed constructors; it does not demand protection against hostile process code, reflection, forged local objects, filesystem attackers or cryptographic substitution. Reject malformed authored GTL at the earliest capable type/raw/lint/validator boundary. F_P external data still requires result-schema and contradiction checks before accepted assessment/closure; raw observations/diagnostics and non-close retry truth may remain. This family owns matching to the seam; ABG plugin/result requirements own returned schemas.

grounding.quote:
A conformance report is scoped to one admitted submitted root identified by
`subjectRef`: its admitted module, program, graph-function, and catalog rows, plus its
declared expected-coverage contract. The GTL validator checks every declaration
reachable from that root and reports required rows missing relative to that
bound coverage contract where the contract carries an applicable inventory
field. For execution declarations, the validator proves declared-reference
completeness and internal membership; the current coverage carrier does not
express a total expected execution-declaration inventory. Product/install
binding selects the authoritative root and complete release manifest. Those
are separate release contracts.

constraints.statement: Check every declaration reachable from the admitted subjectRef root and report required missing rows relative to applicable inventory fields in its bound expected-coverage contract. Execution checks prove declared-reference completeness and membership; authoritative Product/install root and complete release manifest belong to separate release contracts.

conditions: Terms are well typed and named boundaries and effects agree.
Child wire-contract equality requires its admitted language-data relation.

grounding.quote:
For all well-typed terms where the named boundaries and effects agree:

```text
C.compose(C.id, c) == c
C.compose(c, C.id) == c
C.compose(C.compose(a, b), c) == C.compose(a, C.compose(b, c))
workflow.C(GraphFunctionRef<A,B>) preserves the ref's declared A,B contract
C.retry(c, n) preserves the contract of c
C.batch distributes pointwise over C.compose for equal-length ordered task families
fibre substitution preserves C-call spine shape
```

Equality is canonical semantic equality under admitted identity and normalized
declaration data, not host object identity.

The `workflow.C` law does not synthesize a missing wire-level outer-contract
identity. A build may certify equality to the child GraphFunction contract only
when that relation is present as admitted language data.

constraints.statement: For all well-typed terms with agreeing named boundaries and effects: C.id is left/right identity, C.compose is associative, workflow.C preserves the reference-declared A,B, retry preserves its argument contract, batch distributes pointwise over equal-length ordered families, and fibre substitution preserves spine shape. Equality means admitted identity plus normalized canonical semantic data, never host object identity. Child GraphFunction equality requires an admitted outer-contract relation; workflow.C cannot synthesize one.

grounding.quote:
A toolchain is non-conforming when it relies on prose prompting to prevent a
category error that the native type system or GTL validator could reject;
when a bound submitted root can omit a declaration required by its own module,
catalog, or expected-coverage truth; when a runner interprets an unregistered
declaration; or when an invalid program can produce effects before its
diagnostic is emitted.

constraints.statement: A toolchain is nonconforming if it relies on prose to prevent a type/validator-decidable category error, permits root-required module/catalog/coverage declarations to be absent, lets a runner interpret unregistered declarations, or permits invalid effects before diagnostics.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-COMPOSE-002**: Composition shall be associative as a semantic law.

**REQ-L-GTL3-COMPOSE-003**: An identity graph function shall exist that preserves the interface under left and right composition.

**REQ-L-GTL3-COMPOSE-004**: Composed graph functions shall remain replayable. Composition structure and resulting truth shall be reconstructable from declarations plus runtime truth.

**REQ-L-GTL3-COMPOSE-005**: Composition shall propagate and deterministically merge composition-visible metadata such as `effects`, `tags`, and structured declarations.

**REQ-L-GTL3-COMPOSE-006**: Structured declaration merge shall fail closed on conflicting values rather than silently inventing composition semantics.

constraints.statement: Composition is associative, has an interface-preserving left/right identity and stays replayable with structure/truth reconstructible from declarations and runtime truth. Deterministically propagate/merge visible effects, tags and structured declarations; fail closed on conflicting structured values instead of inventing semantics.

exceptions: Explicit contract narrowing may reduce available carried bindings.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-COMPOSE-007**: Composition shall preserve cumulative environment truth immutably. Upstream carried bindings remain available to downstream functions unless composition explicitly narrows the contract.

**REQ-L-GTL3-COMPOSE-008**: Composition shall fail closed when downstream required bindings are absent from the carried environment or structurally mismatch the available carried contracts.

**REQ-L-GTL3-COMPOSE-009**: Composition shall fail closed on conflicting carried output bindings rather than silently overwriting prior environment truth.

constraints.statement: Preserve cumulative carried environment immutably. Upstream bindings remain available unless the composition explicitly narrows the contract. Fail closed for missing downstream requirements, structural mismatch or conflicting carried outputs; never silently overwrite prior environment truth.

conditions: Differently named endpoints need explicit wiring and declared type-law satisfaction.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-COMPOSE-010**: Composition shall distinguish endpoint port
identity from endpoint type contract. Exact name-and-contract composition
shall remain lawful, but it shall not be the only lawful form once explicit
type wiring is declared.

**REQ-L-GTL3-COMPOSE-011**: Type-sensitive composition shall permit
differently named endpoints to compose only when the provided endpoint type
satisfies the required endpoint type through declared GTL type law.

**REQ-L-GTL3-COMPOSE-012**: Type-sensitive composition shall fail closed when
type refs are unknown, composed type obligations are weakened, or explicit
wiring is ambiguous. It shall not infer semantic equivalence from similar
names, tags, schema strings, or prompt prose.

constraints.statement: Distinguish port identity from type contract. Exact name-and-contract composition remains lawful but is not exclusive when explicit wiring is declared. Differently named endpoints compose only when declared GTL type law proves the provided type satisfies the required type. Unknown references, weakened obligations or ambiguous wiring fail closed; similar names/tags/schema strings/prose prove no equivalence.

grounding.quote:
The stable epistemic flow is:

```text
A
  -> transform.C
  -> candidate/evidence refs
  -> evaluate.C
  -> evaluation finding refs
  -> ABG admission
  -> ABG events, ledgers, assurance projection, traversal projection
  -> consequence.C
  -> product read-model interpretation
  -> B or lawful continuation
```

`C` is selected composition notation: the selected `abg.fn_composition`
contract identity for the owning boundary.

constraints.statement: The declared flow is A -> transform.C -> candidate/evidence references -> evaluate.C -> finding references -> ABG admission -> ABG event/ledger/assurance/traversal projections -> consequence.C -> Product read-model interpretation -> B or lawful continuation. Candidate and finding production is not admission.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-002 - Unit.**
`C.of<A,B,Role,Fibre>(stage<A,B,Role,Fibre>) -> C<A,B>` introduces one atomic
C-call leaf. The enclosing `CProgramDeclaration.programRef` supplies program
identity; the leaf supplies role, fibre, arm, and input/output carrier refs.
Together they name one `(program, role, fibre, arm)` census member. The leaf
has one C-call spine and an implementation may realize only its interior.

**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-010 - Implementation matching.** A plugin or handler
binding shall match the enclosing program identity and selected stage role,
fibre, and arm. C input/output carrier continuity is a GTL-validator
judgment. Each implementation separately matches the published carrier
contract of its plugin or handler seam; a uniform engine-plugin transport
carrier is not falsely equated with the domain C carrier ref. Its public type
and admitted carrier shall not provide event emission, traversal selection,
continuation, ledger, or closure authority. ABG admits its result and owns all
resulting runtime truth.

relations.meaning: A matched implementation realizes only the interior of its one declared C-call leaf and supplies no runtime authority.

grounding.quote:
Define the GTL-facing epistemology over the ratified GTL ontology and ABG
runtime ontology without adding a new GTL topology object, ABG runtime carrier,
or execution target.

The notation exists so authors and tools can distinguish what exists from how
it is known. Ontology names the lawful carriers. Epistemology names the
knowledge states over those carriers: candidate production, evaluation
findings, ABG admission, ABG ledger/projection truth, assurance fold,
traversal transition, and downstream consequence projection.

Product ontology remains outside GTL and ABG. A downstream product may define
pressure maps, acceptance lenses, lifecycle registers, and domain read models,
but those meanings are product projections over ABG-admitted facts, not new GTL
or ABG ontology.

relations.meaning: Notation describes epistemic states over the existing ontology without creating carriers; Product interpretations stay projections over ABG facts.

grounding.quote:
**REQ-L-GTL3-C-ALGEBRA-006 - Named workflow lift.**
`workflow.C(GraphFunctionRef<A,B>) -> C<A,B>` is the only constructor that
makes an admitted graph-function traversal one transparent C at its parent
level. The typed `GraphFunctionRef` binds the admitted graph function and the
declared C input/output carriers; the lift preserves that `A,B` pair. Raw
validation proves that the named graph function resolves. Equality between
those carrier refs and a child's published wire contract requires an admitted
outer-contract identity and shall not be inferred when that identity is absent.
The lift yields `sub_traversal` evidence. Anonymous nesting never creates a
frame or monad boundary.

The `workflow.C` law does not synthesize a missing wire-level outer-contract
identity. A build may certify equality to the child GraphFunction contract only
when that relation is present as admitted language data.

residuals.uncertainty: An admitted reference may resolve without a supplied admitted identity equating its carrier pair to the child published wire contract.
